chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Art Tatum and the after-hours piano sessions
summary: He describes after-hours houses where local pianists played in turn before Tatum, who loved whist and beer.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: But I think when we went up to the Union and started jamming up there, that only lasted for about a week, and they told us, you know, to go ahead and jam. Then we started going out and playing wherever we wanted to, and that was during the time also, you know, some of the things that was really beautiful, it was during the time when Tatum was in Los Angeles, too, and they used to have some great sessions with Tatum, but this was when they used to go to after-hours places where there would just be a piano in the place, and the people sold whiskey and beer, and Tatum was an excellent card player -- he loved to play Whist and Pinnacle. At Whist he was really very good.

But you would always see 3 or 4 piano players with Art Tatum, and every one of these houses he would go to, there would be 3 or 4 and it was just like it was unwritten. You would find Eddie Beal with him, you would see Dudley Brooks with him, who else would you see ... whoever thought they could play a little. But you know? It was -- when we used to sit up and look at them and listen to them, and he would be sitting playing cards and drinking beer over there, and so the guy -- they knew what order they should be playing in, you know, it

was like unwritten, but the guy that -- the Lightweight would start off first, and he would play a while, and so they're drinking beer. And so another guy would touch him and he would get up; then he would play.

Now they all are gonna play so they can get to El Presidente, you know, who was Art, and after the 3 of them would play, Art would sit there and drink beer a little while, and he'd get over and he'd jump up to the piano and say Breeee deeee doo. But he was unreal.
